title: A codebook for what medical graders actually disagree about
line: not whether a checklist line is debatable, but what the disagreement is about: seven types, built from 79 hand-read lines
question: A benchmark's checklist lines get scored by physicians who often disagree. A regex can say a line looks debatable. What it cannot say is what two clinicians would be arguing about, which is the thing that decides whether the disagreement is a flaw or the point.
skills: distinguishing a measurable construct from a vague one
data: 79 example-level checklist lines across 56 conversations, every one hand-read
a pool of 1,186 candidate lines awaiting labelling
did: rejected the earlier framing. A 22 November run asked whether a line was debatable and answered with a regex, which measures wording rather than disagreement.
reframed the question so it can be read off a single line: when a reasonable clinician would score this line the other way, what is the disagreement about?
built seven types naming a kind of disagreement, plus an exit code and a residual, from 79 lines read by hand.
wrote a master tie-break, a counterfactual test, so a line that fits two types has a stated rule rather than a coder's preference.
found: the useful question is not how much graders disagree but what about. Disagreement over a clinical fact, over how much to hedge, and over who the patient is are three different problems with three different fixes.

a property that can be read off a single line is labelable at scale. A property that needs the whole conversation is not, which is what makes the reframing the substantive move rather than a wording change.
so_what: published medical AI benchmarks report agreement rates and not what the disagreements are made of, so a 44.6% disagreement rate on one category reads as noise when it may be a category that is genuinely contested.
a codebook with a stated tie-break is the difference between a label set another person can reproduce and one that encodes a single reader's intuition.
calls: one line as the unit of analysis, because it is the unit the benchmark actually scores.
holding the codebook at draft until it is approved, rather than labelling 1,186 lines against a rule set that may still move.
not_shown: the labelling. 1,186 candidate lines are identified and none are labelled with this codebook yet.
no second coder and therefore no reliability statistic. Until there is one, the types are a proposal.
tried: the first version asked whether a line was debatable, which a regex will happily answer and which tells you about adjectives rather than about medicine.
